item.title: Six missing healthcare workers found safe at sea
item.description: The Fiji Navy has confirmed that the six people reported missing at sea in the Lau Group have been found safe, bringing a successful end to a major search and rescue operation. In a statement, the Navy said the six were located about 11 nautical miles southwest of Lakeba by the Goundar Shipping vessel Lomaiviti Princess 12 .
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Navy has confirmed that the six people reported missing at sea in the Lau Group have been found safe, bringing a successful end to a major search and rescue operation.

In a statement, the Navy said the six were located about 11 nautical miles southwest of Lakeba by the Goundar Shipping vessel Lomaiviti Princess 12 .

The Navy thanked mariners and vessels operating in the area for responding quickly to the search effort, with special acknowledgement given to the captain and crew of Lomaiviti Princess 12 for locating and rescuing the missing group.

It also acknowledged the efforts of government agencies, search teams, communities and individuals who worked together during the operation.

The Navy said the successful rescue highlighted the importance of cooperation and vigilance among government agencies and the maritime community.

The six healthcare workers had been reported missing while travelling from Moce to Oneata on a Ministry of Health outreach mission after their vessel developed engine problems and began taking on water.

item.title: Diabetes Fiji calls for national NCD response
item.description: Diabetes Fiji has called for an urgent nationwide response after new health data revealed diabetes and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are reaching unprecedented levels across the country. Speaking on the findings of the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey, Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the latest figures should serve as a wake-up call for government, businesses, civil society, sp
item.content:encoded:
Diabetes Fiji has called for an urgent nationwide response after new health data revealed diabetes and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are reaching unprecedented levels across the country.

Speaking on the findings of the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey, Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the latest figures should serve as a wake-up call for government, businesses, civil society, sporting organisations and faith-based groups.

“In light of alarming epidemiological findings from the recent 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey, Diabetes Fiji is issuing an urgent clarion call to government bodies, corporate entities, civil society organisations, sports federations, and faith-based institutions to forge a united front against the nation’s non-communicable disease (NCD) epidemic,” Mr Marawa said.

The survey found diabetes prevalence had climbed to between 16.5 and 17 per cent, up from 14.6 per cent in 2011.

It also showed 98.5 per cent of adults aged 18 to 69 have at least one risk factor for NCDs, while 47 per cent live with three or more risk factors.

“Over 68 per cent of adults are classified as overweight or obese, with obesity affecting 40 per cent of the population, 70 per cent of whom are women.”

Mr Marawa said the survey also found 36.6 per cent of Fijians had hypertension, with almost half previously unaware they had the condition.

“Crucially, only 21 per cent consume the recommended daily intake of fruits and vegetables.”

“While 30 per cent smoke, 49 per cent consume alcohol and 56 per cent drink kava and they are predominantly males.”

Mr Marawa said the findings underscored the need for a coordinated national effort to reverse the growing NCD epidemic.

item.title: NCD Crisis | Marawa: Diabetes no longer age-related
item.description: Diabetes is increasingly affecting younger Fijians, with cases now being diagnosed in children as young as one year and seven months, according to the latest findings highlighted by Diabetes Fiji. Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey showed the disease was no longer confined to older age groups.
item.content:encoded:
Diabetes is increasingly affecting younger Fijians, with cases now being diagnosed in children as young as one year and seven months, according to the latest findings highlighted by Diabetes Fiji.

Diabetes Fiji executive officer Kini Marawa said the 2025 Fiji NCD STEPS Survey showed the disease was no longer confined to older age groups.

“4.7 per cent of young adults aged 18-29 years now live with diabetes,” Mr Marawa said.

“Tragically, the youngest diagnosed cases with Type 1 diabetes stand at one year and seven months, 11 years old with Type 2, and a stroke recorded in a 12-year-old.”

He said the findings also exposed significant gaps in diagnosis and treatment.

“Among those living with diabetes, only 46.5 per cent are aware of their condition, a mere 33 per cent to 71 per cent receive medical treatment a critically low 6.2 per cent to 21.5 per cent achieve optimal blood glucose control.”

He said the consequences were devastating, with non-communicable diseases responsible for 80 per cent of all deaths in Fiji and between 30 and 40 per cent classified as premature deaths among adults aged 35 to 55.

“Diabetes is also the root cause of 68.5 per cent of end-stage kidney failure cases and 27 per cent of sight-threatening diabetic retinopathy.

Mr Marawa said the survey further found an amputation is performed every 8.5 hours, while 45 per cent of cardiac admissions were linked to life-threatening heart attacks, contributing to seven deaths every day.

item.title: NCD fight ‘overlooked’
item.description: Diabetes Fiji has criticised the Government’s funding priorities, claiming the country’s biggest public health crisis continues to be overlooked despite repeated calls for greater investment in the fight against non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Executive officer Kini Marawa said the organisation was disappointed that its budget submissions and requests for financial assistance had failed to secur
item.content:encoded:
Diabetes Fiji has criticised the Government’s funding priorities, claiming the country’s biggest public health crisis continues to be overlooked despite repeated calls for greater investment in the fight against non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

Executive officer Kini Marawa said the organisation was disappointed that its budget submissions and requests for financial assistance had failed to secure dedicated government funding.

“Diabetes Fiji expresses profound disappointment in the current policy trajectory, which continues to relegate NCDs – our nation’s greatest public health crisis – to a secondary concern,” Mr Marawa said.

“Despite our relentless advocacy, active participation in national budget consultations, and submission of comprehensive, data-driven budget proposals year after year – including throughout the recent financial year – our requests for dedicated financial support have continuously been overlooked and left unaddressed by the government.”

Mr Marawa questioned the Government’s priorities, arguing that economic development could not be sustained without a healthy population.

“Why is public health continually treated as a secondary priority when 80 per cent of our mortality is driven by NCDs? Healthcare must be the primary priority, not an afterthought.”

He also expressed concern that no dedicated budget allocation had been provided to civil society organisations supporting the Ministry of Health and Medical Services.

“Diabetes Fiji notes with concern that the government has failed to allocate a dedicated budgetary line to civil society organisations that directly support the Ministry of Health and Medical Services on the frontlines.”

Despite the funding concerns, Mr Marawa said Diabetes Fiji continued to deliver its Primary Healthcare Screening Program with support from corporate partners, donor agencies and the ministries of Health and Women.

He said the organisation’s focus extended beyond community screening to ensuring patients remained connected to treatment and care through close collaboration with the Health Ministry.

item.title: Compliance check set for project
item.description: The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change is preparing to undertake a compliance inspection of the Natadola Cable Landing Development Project to verify activities on the ground and determine whether environmental approvals, conditions and legal requirements are being followed. A ministry statement said the inspection would be carried out in accordance with its regulatory responsibilities unde
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change is preparing to undertake a compliance inspection of the Natadola Cable Landing Development Project to verify activities on the ground and determine whether environmental approvals, conditions and legal requirements are being followed.

A ministry statement said the inspection would be carried out in accordance with its regulatory responsibilities under the Environment Management Act 2005 (as amended), amid public concerns surrounding the development and its links to a proposed Google ICT facility.

It clarified that the environmental approvals issued for the Natadola Cable Landing Development Project did not amount to approval of a hyperscale Google data centre.

“The assessments submitted to it related to cable landing infrastructure under the Pacific Connect initiative, a regional telecommunications programme establishing subsea cable links between Fiji, the United States, Australia and French Polynesia,” the ministry said.

It indicated community members appeared to be viewing the cable landing works, the proposed Google ICT facility and wider data centre development as one connected project, although the components were assessed separately.

“Three Environmental Management Plan (EMP) applications were lodged, with the Landing Station Facility developed by Staghorn Services Pte Ltd approved with conditions on July 19, 2024.

“The Marine Subsea Cable Landing, developed by Yellowfin Infrastructure Pte Ltd, was approved with conditions on September 23, 2024.”

However, the EMP application for two beach manholes and trenching of conduits leading to the landing station facility was declined on February 5, 2025, due to community concerns, objections and insufficient social survey and consultation information.

They said the cable landing development had neither been applied for nor assessed as a hyperscale data centre, meaning international water consumption figures associated with large data centres were not applicable.

“The ministry remains committed to ensuring that development proposals are assessed transparently and responsibly, with due consideration given to community concerns, environmental protection, and compliance with Fiji’s environmental laws and regulations.”

item.title: Senior PRB officer under investigation
item.description: An independent investigation has been initiated into allegations of abuse of office and the alleged misuse of Public Rental Board (PRB) resources involving a senior official. Minister for Housing and Local Government Maciu Nalumisa confirmed to The Fiji Times the ministry had received formal complaints against the officer.
item.content:encoded:
An independent investigation has been initiated into allegations of abuse of office and the alleged misuse of Public Rental Board (PRB) resources involving a senior official.

Minister for Housing and Local Government Maciu Nalumisa confirmed to The Fiji Times the ministry had received formal complaints against the officer.

Mr Nalumisa said the allegations had not been determined and would be examined through an independent investigation once a panel was formally constituted.

“These allegations have not been determined and are intended to be examined through the independent investigation once the panel has been formally constituted.

“The correspondence received includes allegations concerning the possible use of PRB assets, personnel and staff time for activities said to fall outside PRB’s core functions.

“Whether any such use occurred, whether it was authorised, and whether it involved any personal purpose are matters for the investigation. The ministry and PRB cannot treat those allegations as established facts.”

Mr Nalumisa said the allegations also related to financial and operational controls and the use of PRB assets and resources but stressed no finding of misuse has been made.

He said formal steps had commenced to establish an independent investigation and that terms of reference covering governance, human resources, financial and operational matters had already been prepared.

“Proposed panel members have been approached; however, the ministry is still awaiting their formal confirmation of acceptance.”

On whether the officer would be suspended, Mr Nalumisa said interim administrative arrangements were a matter for the PRB Board.

“Administrative leave, if applied, would be a neutral and precautionary measure and would not constitute disciplinary action or a finding of wrongdoing.”

Attempts to contact the senior officer yesterday through official channels proved futile.

item.title: LDS urges protection of religious freedom
item.description: A wakening of constitutional protections for religious freedom could put Fiji’s social harmony, equality and peaceful coexistence at risk. This was the message from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS) Pacific Area President, Elder Taniela Wakolo, as he urged the Constitutional Review Commission (CRC) to maintain Fiji as a secular state and preserve constitutional protections for
item.content:encoded:
A wakening of constitutional protections for religious freedom could put Fiji’s social harmony, equality and peaceful coexistence at risk.

This was the message from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS) Pacific Area President, Elder Taniela Wakolo, as he urged the Constitutional Review Commission (CRC) to maintain Fiji as a secular state and preserve constitutional protections for religious freedom.

Elder Wakolo said religious freedom was a right that extended beyond people of faith and applied to every citizen.

He said it included the freedom to worship, the freedom not to worship, and the freedom for people of different beliefs to live together with mutual respect and dignity.

“Fiji’s long history of religious diversity had been one of the nation’s strengths, contributing to social harmony and community service across many generations,” he said.

Elder Wakolo said people from many faith traditions had helped build Fiji by serving their neighbours, strengthening families, caring for vulnerable people and contributing to the nation’s wellbeing.

“Constitutional protections allowing people to live according to their sincerely held beliefs should be carefully preserved because they enabled individuals and communities to contribute freely to the common good.”

He said those protections benefited not only religious organisations but society as a whole.

“The measure of religious freedom is not how well it protects the majority. It is how well it protects everyone.”

He said a just and peaceful society ensured that people of every faith, and those of no faith, were treated equally under the law.

Elder Wakolo said people could hold different beliefs while remaining united as citizens, adding that religious freedom created space for respectful dialogue, cooperation and peaceful coexistence.

He said these principles had served Fiji well and should continue to guide the country’s future.

item.title: Six healthcare workers missing at sea in Lau
item.description: A major search and rescue operation is underway in the Lau Waters after six healthcare workers travelling aboard the Ministry of Health and Medical Services vessel, MD Ono-i-Lau, were reported missing while on a medical outreach mission. The team, comprising a Medical Officer, Dental Officer, Charge Nurse, Peer Educator, Health Inspector and Dental Assistant, left Moce at 7am yesterday and was exp
item.content:encoded:
A major search and rescue operation is underway in the Lau Waters after six healthcare workers travelling aboard the Ministry of Health and Medical Services vessel, MD Ono-i-Lau, were reported missing while on a medical outreach mission.

The team, comprising a Medical Officer, Dental Officer, Charge Nurse, Peer Educator, Health Inspector and Dental Assistant, left Moce at 7am yesterday and was expected to reach Oneata after about two hours.

The Ministry of Health confirmed that the vessel’s boat handler was found by a search party from Lakeba this morning and is receiving medical treatment at Lakeba Hospital. The six healthcare workers remain missing.

According to information provided by the boat handler, the vessel’s engine failed before it began taking in water.

The healthcare workers put on life jackets and used the vessel’s wooden floor planks as flotation devices.

The boat handler then swam towards Aiwa Island in an effort to obtain mobile phone reception, leaving the medical team safely secured and without injuries at that time.

When the vessel failed to arrive in Oneata as scheduled, the district nurse alerted Lakeba Sub-Divisional Hospital, prompting the immediate mobilisation of search teams yesterday afternoon.

The Ministry said it had been working closely with the Fiji Police Force, the Fiji Navy Rescue Coordinating Centre, the Office of the Commissioner Eastern and other partner agencies over the past 24 hours.

Command centres have been activated at Lakeba Sub-Divisional Hospital and the Eastern Health Divisional Office to coordinate the emergency response.

Alerts have also been issued to all eight villages in Lakeba, as well as community leaders through district nurses in Nayau, Vanuavatu and Moala, and the Lomaloma medical team.

The Ministry said it had prioritised informing the next of kin of the six healthcare workers and would continue providing updates as more information became available.

It is appealing to seafarers, mariners and coastal communities travelling through the Lakeba–Oneata passage to remain vigilant and report any sightings that may assist search efforts.
